question: From which country is the power of judicial review taken in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of judicial review in the Indian Constitution is derived from the Constitution of the **United States of America (USA).**
 
• Judicial review refers to the power of the judiciary to interpret the constitutionality of laws and executive actions.
 
• In the USA, the concept was established in the landmark case of **Marbury v. Madison** (1803).
 
• It ensures that the laws passed by the legislature and actions taken by the executive are in accordance with the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**

 
 
• It is a process under which executive or legislative actions are subject to review by the judiciary.
 
• It is an essential function of the judiciary to safeguard the supremacy of the Constitution and to protect the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• In India, judicial review is considered a basic feature of the Constitution, which cannot be amended or taken away by the Parliament.
 
• Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution provide the basis for judicial review of legislative and executive actions.
 
 
 
• **Marbury v. Madison (1803)**
 
 
• This case is significant in American constitutional history as it established the principle of judicial review in the United States.
 
• The case was decided by the Supreme Court under Chief Justice John Marshall.
 
• The ruling declared that the Supreme Court had the power to nullify an act of Congress if it was found to be in conflict with the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Indian Constitution and Judicial Review**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution explicitly confers the power of judicial review on the judiciary through Articles 13, 32, 131-136, 143, 226, and 246.
 
• The Constitution of India provides a system of checks and balances to ensure that no organ of the government exceeds its powers.
 
• Judicial review in India plays a critical role in maintaining the rule of law and ensuring the protection of fundamental rights.
